# Implementation checklist: chat1 — how Ensemble shows things to the owner

## Goal

Change what the owner sees, not what Ensemble does next. Chat With AI becomes a conversation (cards, questions, the owner's messages and the stage AI's replies). Notifications becomes the log, with every entry naming its task. One live strip answers “is it running?”. Every card follows one lifecycle, and cards, warnings and refusals use plain words.

## Verification

### Behaviour to confirm (by reading the code)

- [x] The host builds the transcript through `isConversationEntryV1`. `activity`, `outcome` and the listed old status formats are excluded. User messages, questions, untyped replies and unknown kinds are included.
- [x] Every writer listed in Step 3 sets `kind`, and `traceDecisionOperationV1` writes no `Progress:` line.
- [x] Each hidden kind of line has a Notifications entry that names the task (Step 5), and `terminalEntryFor` includes the settle reason for failed and refused operations.
- [x] The strip is fed by a `runStrip` message built from `taskOperations`. It shows the label, model, start time and latest activity, and is hidden when nothing runs.
- [x] Settled decisions, answered interactions, settled questions and settled open-items forms render as read-only cards with no inputs. The “Answered: … / Resuming…” rendering and the separate Recorded, Dismissed and Withdrawn lines are gone from the transcript.
- [x] Each card header is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded`. Expand choices are saved per card and per card state, in a bounded list.
- [x] Every Dismiss handler reports back to the webview. On failure, the card's controls are enabled again and its reason shows.
- [x] No string the owner can see contains `duplicateRejected`, `observed-unattributed` or “changed index paths”. The one-cycle option label ends “(one cycle, then stops)”.
- [x] The seven commands in Step 23 call their pop-ups again, and `chatChoiceConversionsV1.test.ts` pins them as pop-ups.

### Publish Checks hand-off

- [ ] **Owner step: confirm Publish Checks ran `pnpm run verify` — Priority: LOW.** <!-- ensemble:excluded -->
  - **What:** the expected command is `pnpm run verify`, the project's `verify` script. It runs `check-types` (including `packages/*`), `lint` (`eslint src`), `test` (the unit tests, including the new and updated tests from Steps 7, 17, 22 and 24) and `verify:workflow-safety`.
  - **Why:** nothing in the project shows whether an `ensemble.publishVerificationCommands` value applies to this window (there is no `.vscode/settings.json`, and user and machine settings can't be seen from the project), so which command ran is not confirmed.
  - **How:** open `.ensemble/2026-11-02_task_3/publish-review.md` and find “Commands that ran”. Check that `verify` (or the four scripts above) is listed and passed. If it is not listed, run `pnpm run verify` in the repo root yourself.
  - **If it fails:** a listed command failed, or `verify` is missing and your own run fails.
  - **Priority:** LOW — failures are loud and can be rerun. Skipping it is acceptable; the trade-off is shipping without the type, lint and unit-test checks.
- [ ] **Owner step: build the extension and load the chat panel — Priority: LOW.** <!-- ensemble:excluded -->
  - **What:** run `pnpm run compile` (type check, lint and the esbuild bundle).
  - **Why:** `verify` does not bundle, and the chat's webview script is emitted from a template literal where one stray escape stops the whole panel script from parsing.
  - **How:** run `pnpm run compile`, then run Developer: Reload Window and open any task's Chat With AI.
  - **If it fails:** the build errors, or the chat stays on its loading placeholder.
  - **Priority:** LOW — a failure shows at once. Skipping it is acceptable; the trade-off is risking a chat panel that never loads, which is loud, not silent.

### Owner checks (bugs5 re-tests first)

- [ ] **bugs5 item 19: Dismiss doesn't look like the main action — Priority: LOW.** <!-- ensemble:excluded -->
  - **What:** on a decision card, a question card and the AI Models view, Dismiss is grey (secondary) and sits left of the action button, in both light and dark themes.
  - **Why:** every card's controls in this task build on that style.
  - **How:** open a task that has an open card in Chat With AI. Switch themes with Preferences: Color Theme.
  - **If it fails:** Dismiss is blue (primary), or it sits on the right.
  - **Priority:** LOW — visible at a glance. Skipping it is acceptable; the trade-off is a possible mis-click on Dismiss, which runs nothing.
- [ ] **bugs5 item 21: Dismiss on the idle “checklist flagged unreliable” card sticks — Priority: LOW.** <!-- ensemble:excluded -->
  - **What:** Dismiss hides the card, and it stays hidden until a new round flags the checklist again.
  - **Why:** this was the “Dismiss does nothing” case the design rules out.
  - **How:** on a task whose checklist is flagged unreliable, press Dismiss. Run Developer: Reload Window, then reopen the chat.
  - **If it fails:** the card is back after the reload with no new round in between.
  - **Priority:** LOW — visible. Skipping it is acceptable; the trade-off is another press of Dismiss.
- [ ] **bugs5 item 6: no stale model named before a model starts — Priority: LOW.** <!-- ensemble:excluded -->
  - **What:** while a review runs its checks, the Notifications row and the new chat strip say the model has not started yet. They don't name the previous round's model.
  - **Why:** the strip reuses that wording.
  - **How:** start a review on a task and watch the Notifications row and the strip in the first seconds.
  - **If it fails:** the previous round's model is named before any model starts.
  - **Priority:** LOW — misleading but visible. Skipping it is acceptable; the trade-off is a wrong model name for a few seconds.
- [ ] **bugs5 item 13: Publish Checks show as running at once — Priority: LOW.** <!-- ensemble:excluded -->
  - **What:** starting Publish Checks shows them running within about 2 seconds. The chat never says “no command has started yet”.
  - **Why:** the strip replaces the old start lines, so this re-tests bugs5's fix in its new place.
  - **How:** on a task in Publish, start Publish Checks and watch Chat With AI.
  - **If it fails:** nothing shows for several seconds, or the “not started” line appears while the checks run.
  - **Priority:** LOW — visible. Skipping it is acceptable; the trade-off is some doubt about whether the checks started.
- [ ] **Nothing that needs the owner is hidden (covers Step 2) — Priority: HIGH.** <!-- ensemble:excluded -->
  - **What:** in bugs5's chat, every user message, question, stage-AI reply and card in `chat-v1.json` is visible.
  - **Why:** the new filter hides lines by their format, and a wrong match hides a message silently.
  - **How:** in a terminal, run `jq` with the filter `[.[] | select(.kind == null) | .text[0:60]]` on `.ensemble/2026-11-01_task_1/chat-v1.json`. Every listed entry that is not a Started, Resumed, Progress, Ended, Recorded, Dismissed or Withdrawn status line must appear in bugs5's Chat With AI.
  - **If it fails:** a reply or question in the file is missing from the chat.
  - **Priority:** HIGH — a hidden question or reply goes unnoticed, and the owner never sees what the AI said or asked.
- [ ] **Every hidden line has a Notifications entry (covers Step 5) — Priority: HIGH.** <!-- ensemble:excluded -->
  - **What:** each event the chat stops showing has one Notifications entry that names its task: an automatic start with its trigger, a round's end with its outcome, a recorded answer, a dismissal and a withdrawal.
  - **Why:** Notifications becomes the only log of these events.
  - **How:** on a scratch task, let an automatic start happen, run Apply Review to its end, answer one card and dismiss another. Then look for each event in Notifications.
  - **If it fails:** an event appears nowhere.
  - **Priority:** HIGH — the history is lost silently, and nothing points to the gap later.
- [ ] **The chat shows conversation only — Priority: LOW.** <!-- ensemble:excluded -->
  - **What:** bugs5's Chat With AI shows its 6 cards (finished ones collapsed) and the owner's messages, not around 100 status lines.
  - **Why:** this is the core outcome of bugs6 item 8.
  - **How:** on the new build, open bugs5's Chat With AI and scroll through it.
  - **If it fails:** Started, Progress, Ended, Recorded or Auto-starting lines still show.
  - **Priority:** LOW — visible at once. Skipping it is acceptable; the trade-off is a cluttered chat, not lost data.
- [ ] **The live strip works however a run starts (covers Step 6) — Priority: LOW.** <!-- ensemble:excluded -->
  - **What:** the strip appears within seconds, updates in place, and disappears when the run ends. The result shows as a card or a Notifications entry, not a chat line.
  - **Why:** this meets bugs3 item 12 and bugs4 item 33 for every way a run starts.
  - **How:** start Publish Checks once from a card option and once from Fast Forward, and watch the chat.
  - **If it fails:** no strip appears, several strips stack up, or the strip stays after the run ends.
  - **Priority:** LOW — visible. Skipping it is acceptable; the trade-off is doubt about whether something runs.
- [ ] **A retry loop adds no chat entries — Priority: LOW.** <!-- ensemble:excluded -->
  - **What:** during repeated automatic rounds, the chat gains no new entries until a card is raised. Only the strip changes.
  - **Why:** this was the shape behind bugs5's 200 entries.
  - **How:** let Fast Forward run several rounds on a scratch task, and compare the chat before and after.
  - **If it fails:** new status lines appear in the chat.
  - **Priority:** LOW — visible. Skipping it is acceptable; the trade-off is some clutter.
- [ ] **Cards collapse, expand, and survive a reload — Priority: LOW.** <!-- ensemble:excluded -->
  - **What:** an answered card collapses to one line with the chosen option; a dismissed card collapses with “dismissed”; clicking the line expands and collapses the full read-only card; after a reload, finished cards stay collapsed and a card expanded by hand stays expanded; a new card arrives expanded and the chat scrolls to it.
  - **Why:** this is bugs6 item 6's lifecycle.
  - **How:** answer one card and dismiss another, toggle both, then run Developer: Reload Window. Then trigger a new card.
  - **If it fails:** a finished card disappears, loses its content or shows live buttons, or a choice is forgotten after the reload.
  - **Priority:** LOW — visible. Skipping it is acceptable; the trade-off is a messier chat, never a wrong action.
- [ ] **The card toggle works by keyboard and screen reader (covers Step 12) — Priority: LOW.** <!-- ensemble:excluded -->
  - **What:** Tab reaches each card's line, and Enter or Space toggles it. A screen reader announces it as a button that is expanded or collapsed.
  - **Why:** collapsing must never hide an open card's options from these users.
  - **How:** in Chat With AI, use only the keyboard, with a screen reader (for example NVDA or VoiceOver) running.
  - **If it fails:** the line can't be reached or toggled, or its state isn't announced.
  - **Priority:** LOW — the failure is obvious when tried. Skipping it is acceptable; the trade-off is that keyboard and screen-reader use stays unchecked.
- [ ] **Complete Task refused while Commit & Push waits — Priority: LOW.** <!-- ensemble:excluded -->

  - **How:** start Commit & Push on a scratch task and leave its confirmation unanswered. Then run Complete Task.
  - **If it fails:** the raw code shows, or there are two entries, or there is no way to reach the card.
  - **Priority:** LOW — loud. Skipping it is acceptable; the trade-off is a confusing message, not lost data.
- [ ] **Converted confirmations do exactly what the pop-ups did (covers Step 23) — Priority: HIGH.** (Superseded 2026-11-03: the confirmations stay pop-ups.) <!-- ensemble:excluded -->
  - **What:** confirming a revert in the chat reverts exactly what the old dialog's button did. Dismissing it changes nothing. Reset Chat History clears the chat only when confirmed.
  - **Why:** these answers delete or overwrite work.
  - **How:** on a scratch task, make a stage change, run View Stage Changes, choose revert, and dismiss the card; check that `git status` is unchanged. Repeat, and confirm this time; check that `git diff` shows the revert. Do the same with Reset Chat History.
  - **If it fails:** files change on Dismiss, they don't revert on confirm, or the chat is cleared without confirming.
  - **Priority:** HIGH — work is lost or kept silently, in the owner's own repo.
